title: Onboard curation rules and compact change fragment generator
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduce onboarding curation rule set to validate and normalize model metadata at ingest
Add compact change-fragment generator which emits terse changelog fragments for release assembly
Expose a CLI hook 'redwood model fragment' used by the release pipeline to assemble concise release notes
description: Context and motivation: Onboarding flow currently produces verbose, noisy changelogs and inconsistent metadata validation which creates downstream churn for release note authors and QA. This PR adds a small, focused curation rules engine plus a compact change-fragment generator so releases can be composed from minimal, human-readable fragments. Design summary: 1) curation rules: YAML-driven rule set (onboard/curation/rules.yaml) that normalizes common fields (semantic_family, primary_tokenizer, default_seq_len), enforces required provenance tags, and adds derived compatibility hints; rules run as part of onboard lint and produce a machine-readable remediation summary. 2) compact change fragments: a delta generator that takes model profile diffs (profile hashes + annotated metrics) and emits short fragment objects (title, scope, delta-bullet) optimized for human consumption and automated assembly. The fragment generator uses a heuristic prioritizer: prefer perf regressions > model-compat metadata breaks > semver bump, collapse low-impact numeric drift into an aggregated note. 3) release annotator CLI: lightweight binary (cli/release_fragmenter.py) that converts fragments into templated release lines and uploads them to the release-assembler service. Implementation highlights: - rules.yaml with predicate language and fixers; small rule runtime written in Python with a compact DSL (onboard/curation/runtime.py). - compact_diff_generator.py computes fingerprint-aware diffs to avoid repeating noisy histogram deltas; uses cosine similarity on tokenization signature to detect tokenizer-equivalent variants. - tests: new unit tests verifying common regressions, plus integration smoke test in tests/integration/test_fragment_workflow.py. Backwards compatibility and rollout: curation rules default to 'warn' mode on first rollout; onboarding pipeline emits both original verbose changelog and compact fragments under a feature flag (registry.feature.compact_fragments). After two weeks of production observations we flip to 'enforce' on high-confidence rules. QA and validation: added a small dataset of 12 model onboarding examples (tests/fixtures) and a nightly job that samples new onboards and validates fragment divergence. CI: initial run surfaced a flakey test in tests/test_fragmenter.py related to timezone-sensitive timestamps; fixed by making timestamps monotonic in the test harness. Security/Privacy: no runtime secrets added; fragments purposely omit customer identifying fields and only include model metadata and metric deltas. Rollout Plan: merge to main, enable feature flag for 10% of onboards, monitor 'fragment use rate' and 'manual edits to release notes' metrics in Console. If false positives exceed threshold, revert to warn-only mode and iterate on heuristics. Related: ENG-4219 (onboard QA policy), ENG-4370 (release pipeline integration).
